title: useEffect: Side Effects and the Outside World

subChunks.title: useEffect: Side Effects and the Outside World
subChunks.hookHtml: Components render UI from data. But what about operations that reach outside the component — fetching from an API, reading localStorage, starting a timer, subscribing to a WebSocket? These are side effects: actions that touch the world beyond React's render cycle. useEffect is the hook that manages them safely.
subChunks.explanationHtml:
What is a side effect?

A side effect is anything a component does that isn't "take props and state → return JSX". Examples:

  • Fetching data from an API
  • Setting the document title
  • Starting or stopping a timer
  • Subscribing to a WebSocket or event listener
  • Reading/writing localStorage

Side effects don't belong directly in the render function — they run on every render, including intermediate ones, causing duplicated calls or infinite loops.

useEffect syntax

import { useEffect } from 'react';

useEffect(() => {
  // Side effect code goes here
}, [dependencies]);

useEffect takes two arguments: an effect function and a dependency array.

The dependency array — the most important part

// 1. No array — runs after EVERY render (rarely what you want):
useEffect(() => {
  console.log('Runs after every render');
});

// 2. Empty array — runs ONCE after the first render (mount):
useEffect(() => {
  console.log('Runs once on mount');
}, []);

// 3. With dependencies — runs after mount AND whenever a dep changes:
useEffect(() => {
  console.log('userId changed:', userId);
}, [userId]);

Vex: "The dependency array is a contract: 'this effect depends on these values.' If you use a value inside the effect, it must be in the array. ESLint's exhaustive-deps rule enforces this. If you find yourself wanting to omit a dependency to 'avoid re-running', that's a design smell — you probably need a different structure."

Cleanup functions

If your effect sets up a subscription or timer, it must tear it down when the component unmounts (or before the next run). Return a cleanup function:

useEffect(() => {
  const id = setInterval(() => {
    setTick(t => t + 1);
  }, 1000);

  // This runs when the component unmounts or before the next effect:
  return () => clearInterval(id);
}, []); // Empty array: start once, clear on unmount

Without cleanup, the interval would keep running after the component unmounts — causing state updates on an unmounted component and eventually a memory leak.

Setting the document title — a safe first effect

function QuestPage({ questTitle }) {
  useEffect(() => {
    document.title = `${questTitle} — Arcane Academy`;

    return () => {
      document.title = 'Arcane Academy';
    };
  }, [questTitle]); // Re-run whenever questTitle changes

  return <h1>{questTitle}</h1>;
}

What useEffect is not for

// ❌ Unnecessary effect — this is just a derived value:
const [filtered, setFiltered] = useState([]);
useEffect(() => {
  setFiltered(items.filter(i => i.done));
}, [items]);

// ✅ Compute it directly — no effect needed:
const filtered = items.filter(i => i.done);

storyBeats.text: Vex holds up a component diagram. Inside the render box, everything is clean. Outside it: timers, network requests, browser APIs. She draws a boundary between them.

storyBeats.speaker: Vex the Interface Weaver
storyBeats.text: A component's render function must be pure. Fetching data, setting timers, reading localStorage — these are side effects. They touch the world outside React. useEffect is the designated place to run them safely, after the render is committed to the screen.

storyBeats.speaker: Effect with cleanup

subChunks.guidedPracticeHtml:
Build a <PageTitleSync title /> component. It should use useEffect to set document.title to the value of the title prop every time title changes. When the component unmounts, reset document.title to 'Arcane Academy'.

Also render the title in an <h1 data-testid="heading">.

subChunks.soloPracticeHtml: Build a <CountdownTimer seconds /> component from scratch. It takes a seconds prop (initial countdown value). Every second, the displayed count decreases by 1. When it reaches 0, display Time's up! instead of a number. Use useEffect for the interval and make sure you clean it up.
subChunks.feynmanPrompt: Explain useEffect's dependency array to a colleague. What does it control? What are the three different behaviours depending on whether the array is absent, empty, or contains values? What breaks when you use a value inside an effect but leave it out of the dependency array?

questions.prompt: What does passing an empty array `[]` as useEffect's second argument cause?
options: The effect runs once after the first render and never again
The effect runs after every render
The effect runs before the first render
questions.answer: The effect runs once after the first render and never again
questions.explanation: An empty dependency array tells React 'this effect has no dependencies — nothing can cause it to re-run.' It fires once after the initial render (mount) and the cleanup runs once when the component unmounts. This is the correct pattern for one-time setup like subscribing to a WebSocket or fetching initial data.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of the function returned from a useEffect callback?
options: It runs when the component unmounts or before the next effect run — used to cancel subscriptions and clear timers
It runs before the effect to set up preconditions
It is a callback React calls with the effect's result
It tells React whether to re-run the effect
questions.answer: It runs when the component unmounts or before the next effect run — used to cancel subscriptions and clear timers
questions.explanation: The cleanup function prevents memory leaks and stale subscriptions. React calls it in two situations: when the component unmounts, and before re-running the effect (if dependencies changed). Always return a cleanup from effects that set up subscriptions, intervals, or event listeners.

options: [userId] — the effect must re-run whenever userId changes
No array — re-fetch on every render
questions.answer: [userId] — the effect must re-run whenever userId changes
questions.explanation: The effect uses userId, so it belongs in the dependency array. Without it, the effect would only run on mount and the displayed user would never update when userId changes.

questions.prompt: A component filters a list of items for display using useEffect to set filtered state. What is the problem?
options: It creates an unnecessary extra render — filtered is a derived value that can be computed directly in the component body
The filter function mutates the original array
Missing cleanup will cause a memory leak
questions.answer: It creates an unnecessary extra render — filtered is a derived value that can be computed directly in the component body
questions.explanation: Storing derived data in state adds a wasted render cycle: items changes → effect runs → setFiltered → another render. Instead, compute inline: const filtered = items.filter(i => i.done). This is synchronous, always up-to-date, and requires no effect.
